title: If You'd Invested $1,000 in ExxonMobil 1 Year Ago, Here's How Much You'd Have Today - The Globe and Mail
content: A $1,000 investment in ExxonMobil a year ago would be worth $1,432 today. Higher oil prices and stronger refining margins have boosted Exxon's earnings amid the conflict in Iran. Investments in cost-efficient assets aim to keep Exxon profitable even if oil prices retreat. Since the start of the year, the conflict in Iran has disrupted oil and gas markets, created supply bottlenecks, and driven oil prices higher. These disruptions have been a tailwind for oil and gas producers. As a result, if you had invested $1,000 in ExxonMobil(NYSE:XOM) stock one year ago, that investment would be worth $1,432 today. Missed AI’s "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we’re only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » This year has been volatile for the oil and gas industry, as the Iran conflict has disrupted the Straight of Hormuz, through which over 20 million barrels per day of crude oil, condensate, and refined petroleum products pass. For ExxonMobil, the disruptions have been a boon. Brent crude oil has traded as high as $120 per barrel and has stayed above $70 per barrel since the conflict began. This has driven strong upstream growth, but an even bigger driver is downstream refined fuels, where margins (crack spreads) have surged. For ExxonMobil, the world's largest non-state-owned refiner, this translates into significant downstream profits. Through Sept. 30, Exxon's upstream earnings jumped 16% to $20.8 billion, driven by higher crude oil prices. Meanwhile, its downstream energy products earnings have surged 181% to $11.4 billion, driven by strong refining margins. ExxonMobil has taken steps over the past several years to invest in cost-efficient, "advantaged assets" that help drive down the cost per barrel for oil. By focusing on these highly profitable assets, the company aims to lower its breakeven cost per barrel to $35 by 2027 and $30 by 2030, so even if oil prices retreat from their current highs, Exxon can keep profiting. title: What Would Cheaper Fuel Mean For Exxon Mobil Stock? - Trefis
content: For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com. Over the past twelve months, Exxon Mobil (XOM) stock returned 45.9%, compared with 12.2% for the S&P 500. On its October 30, 2026 call, management said the Middle East conflict had left diesel and gasoline in short supply and prices higher, and guessed that a return to normal would take well through 2027. Exxon still plans $20 billion of buybacks in 2027, assuming reasonable market conditions. So what would normal fuel markets mean for Exxon’s cash? If free cash flow fell back to the level of a year earlier, Exxon would give up about $19.2 billion a year. The company generated $43.0 billion of free cash flow in the four quarters to September 2026, compared with $23.8 billion in the four quarters to September 2025. That gap is not all from fuel: on the call, management said the fighting also constrained crude supplies. That lower level would still cover the $17.3 billion Exxon paid in dividends over the past twelve months, but it would leave only about $6.5 billion toward the 2027 buyback plan. The stock would also look less cheap. Exxon trades at 17.3 times its latest twelve months of earnings, against 21.9 for the S&P 500. Priced on the $30.0 billion Exxon earned in the year to September 2025, today’s market value would be about 23 times earnings. Exxon has tapped its balance sheet to fill similar gaps before. In the weaker year to September 2025, the company still bought back $20.7 billion of shares, and its cash and short-term investments fell from $26.9 billion to $13.8 billion. On the October 30 call, management said that when times are tougher, Exxon does not pull back from its commitment and uses the balance sheet to supplement it. The cash pile is smaller now, at $12.2 billion on September 30, 2026, but Exxon’s debt is light. At the year-earlier level of free cash flow, the roughly $13.5 billion of the 2027 buyback not covered after dividends would exceed that cash. Total debt equals 4.9% of Exxon’s market value, against 19.5% for the S&P 500. Over the past twelve months, operating income covered interest expense 55.6 times, and management said Exxon cut its net debt by more than $9 billion in the third quarter of 2026. A return to the cash flow of the year to September 2025 would test how long Exxon funds its buybacks from the balance sheet, not whether it can pay its debts. The first sign will come from Exxon itself. Instead of holding a December plan event, management said the company will reaffirm key 2027 planning metrics in a press release before the end of 2026, once the board approves the plan. Management also announced a fourth-quarter dividend of $1.07 per share. A return to normal fuel prices would test Exxon’s buyback plan well before it tested the company. Free cash flow against the total dividend bill is the figure to watch when Exxon reports its fourth quarter, expected in January 2027. You don’t have to bet on one stock to earn. ExxonMobil is an integrated energy and chemical company with operations spanning the oil and natural gas value chain. Its businesses explore for and produce crude oil and natural gas, refine and market fuels, and manufacture chemicals and other specialty products. ExxonMobil participates in nearly every stage of bringing energy and materials to market. Integration across these stages can help balance results, since different businesses respond differently to changes in commodity prices. For example, lower crude prices can weigh on production income while easing feedstock costs for refining and chemicals. That diversification is a defining feature of the companys business model. ExxonMobils upstream business explores for and produces crude oil and natural gas across major producing regions. Key areas include the Permian Basin in the United States, among the most productive oil regions in the world, and large offshore developments in South America. These regions are known for resources that can be developed efficiently, supporting production growth. Elevated crude prices can support revenue from producing assets, since higher prices increase the value of each barrel produced. Upstream results depend on production volumes, oil and gas prices, and operating costs. The companys portfolio of long-lived assets allows it to plan development over many years, supporting steady production as new projects come online. ExxonMobil has given final approval to a major new offshore development in South America, a project expected to add future production capacity. Final approval marks the point at which a company commits to building a project, following years of exploration, appraisal, and engineering. Offshore developments of this scale typically involve floating production facilities, subsea wells, and extensive infrastructure. The project reinforces the companys growth in a producing region known for its lower-cost resources. Large projects require substantial capital and take several years to complete before production begins. Once operating, they can provide long-term production that supports cash flow over many years. Progress on this development will be closely followed. Beyond production, ExxonMobil refines crude oil into fuels and markets products including gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, and lubricants. Its chemical business manufactures petrochemical feedstocks and materials used in a wide range of consumer and industrial applications, from packaging and automotive parts to construction materials. Refining results depend on the difference between crude oil costs and the prices of refined products, which can vary with demand and supply conditions. Recent commentary has highlighted strong refining results across the industry. Chemical demand follows industrial activity and consumer spending. Together, these downstream businesses add diversification and capture value from the companys production, contributing significantly to overall results. ExxonMobil also pursues lower-emission solutions, including carbon capture and storage, hydrogen, and lower-emission fuels. Carbon capture and storage involves capturing carbon dioxide from industrial sources and storing it underground, helping industrial customers reduce emissions. Hydrogen can serve as a lower-emission fuel and feedstock for industry, while lower-emission fuels offer alternatives for transportation. These efforts draw on the companys expertise in large-scale engineering, geology, and chemical processing. As industries and governments pursue emissions goals, demand for these solutions can grow. For ExxonMobil, lower-emission businesses represent an additional area of development alongside its core oil, gas, and chemical operations. The company also raised its dividend and announced a large share repurchase program for next year. For readers who follow Oil and Gas Stocks, ExxonMobil is the largest US energy company and a bellwether for the integrated oil sector on the NYSE Composite. Reported earnings doubled compared with the same quarter last year and also rose from the second quarter. Adjusted earnings per share comfortably beat analyst expectations. Cash flow from operating activities was very strong, and free cash flow remained high, allowing the company to fund large cash returns to investors while continuing to reduce net debt. The Energy Products segment, which includes refining and fuels marketing, more than doubled its adjusted earnings from the second quarter. Higher industry margins drove most of the gain, as global disruptions tightened fuel supplies. ExxonMobil also delivered excellent operational performance. Its US Gulf Coast refineries ran at full crude-unit utilization, and diesel production from those refineries reached one of its highest levels on record. Investments such as the Beaumont refinery expansion have significantly increased its distillate output in recent years. Upstream earnings declined from the second quarter, mainly because of lower crude oil prices and accelerated production-entitlement effects in Guyana. Total oil and gas production was broadly steady from the prior quarter. For the year to date, upstream earnings improved on higher prices and production growth in Guyana, the Permian Basin and Golden Pass LNG, partly offset by disruptions affecting Middle East output. ExxonMobil reached major cumulative production milestones at both Guyana and the Kearl oil sands operation in Canada, as well as at its PNG LNG project. It also assumed operatorship of the Papua LNG project and agreed to increase its stakes in LNG projects in Papua New Guinea and Mozambique. Chemical Products earnings declined from the prior quarter as margins weakened, though higher volumes of high-value products helped. Specialty Products earnings increased on stronger basestock margins and cost savings. The company declared a higher fourth-quarter dividend, extending a streak of annual dividend increases that stretches back a remarkably long time. Very few companies in the S&P index have a longer record. ExxonMobil also announced a large share repurchase program for next year, subject to market conditions. During the third quarter, it distributed a significant amount of cash through dividends and share repurchases. Management highlighted substantial structural cost savings achieved since before the pandemic. These savings, combined with high-return investments and technology, have raised the company's earnings power. Management argues these are lasting improvements rather than simply the result of favorable prices. ExxonMobil continued to advance carbon capture and storage projects, including a startup with steelmaker Nucor and approval for a new carbon storage project. These efforts aim to build new revenue streams while helping industrial customers reduce emissions. ExxonMobil operates across the full energy value chain, from oil and gas production to refining, chemicals and specialty lubricants. This integration helps smooth results through commodity cycles. In the third quarter, softer crude prices hurt upstream earnings, but the same conditions helped refining margins, which more than made up the difference. This balance is a key reason integrated oil companies tend to generate steadier cash flow than pure exploration and production companies, whose results depend more directly on oil and gas prices. Guyana and the Permian Basin are ExxonMobil's most important growth engines. Guyana offers large, low-cost offshore oil production, while the Permian provides flexible onshore output that can be adjusted more quickly. Together they are expected to drive much of the company's production growth over the coming years. ExxonMobil has reduced net debt significantly so far this year, strengthening an already solid balance sheet. A low debt level gives the company flexibility to keep investing in growth projects and returning cash to investors even if commodity prices weaken. Oil and gas price volatility, refining margin normalization, Middle East supply disruptions, project execution and policy changes are the main risks. Elevated refining margins tend to be cyclical and may not last. Key indicators include refining margins, Guyana and Permian production growth, LNG project progress, next year's capital spending plans and the pace of share repurchases. ExxonMobil's third quarter showed the strength of its integrated model, with refining gains more than offsetting softer upstream results. A higher dividend, a large repurchase plan and steady production growth support its position as a leading oil and gas company, while commodity cycles remain the key swing factor. title: Oil Still Above $85, EOG Up 41% in a Year: Is the Stock Still a Buy? - The Globe and Mail
content: EOG Resources Inc. EOG has jumped 40.8% over the past year, outpacing the 20.9% growth of the industry’s composite stocks, and 40.4% and 37.1% improvements of its peers Exxon Mobil CorporationXOM and Chevron CorporationCVX, respectively. The outperformance might reflect strong market confidence in EOG’s prospects, especially when the pricing scenario of oil is extremely favorable. However, for investment conclusions, one should have a thorough assessment of the company’s fundamentals, growth potential and prevailing market conditions. West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude is trading at more than $85 per barrel, according to data from oilprice.com, owing to the persisting tensions in the Middle East. With EOG generating a significant proportion of revenues from crude oil and condensate, the high price of the commodity is extremely favorable for the leading oil and gas exploration and production company, like other energy giants, such as XOM and CVX. The prolific multi-basin portfolio of EOG Resources comprises as much as 12 billion barrels of oil equivalent resources. With oil prices likely to remain high, per the U.S. Energy Information Administration, the company, with its diversified set of oil & gas assets, is expected to continue generating handsome cash flows for its shareholders. EOG is also well-positioned to gain on the rising demand for natural gas from increasing exports of LNG and massive consumption of electricity by AI data centers. The company has a low exposure to debt capital and hence can rely on its balance sheet to sail through all the business cycles efficiently. Compared to composite stocks in the industry, EOG has lower debt exposure, reflected in debt to capitalization of 19.31% compared with the industry’s 23.54%. To highlight the upstream player’s strong commitment to return shareholders’ capital, the company has never suspended or lowered dividend payments. In fact, EOG has been paying dividends for 28 years and plans to reward investors with $2.3 billion of regular dividend payments next year. Coming to the valuation story, EOG is currently considered cheap on a relative basis, with the stock trading at a 5.27x trailing 12-month Enterprise Value to Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization (EV/EBITDA), which is a discount compared with the broader industry average of 8.51x. EOG also appears cheaper compared to integrated giants such as XOM and CVX, which are currently trading at 7.87x and 6.80x trailing 12-month EV/EBITDA, respectively. Despite its strong share-price performance, EOG continues to trade at a discount to its industry peers, suggesting further upside potential. Its favorable fundamentals and attractive valuation make it worth considering. EOG currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). With ImmunityBio (IBRX) shares up more than 200% this year, founder Patrick Soon-Shiong has outlined plans to unveil decades of privately funded research at NantWorks over the next 12 months, spanning cancer therapies, AI chips and satellite tech. IBRX stock tumbled 9% on Thursday to $6.07, with shares down 30% for the week and tracking their worst week in nearly two years. Soon-Shiong said on X: “I began the release of our stealth, self-funded programs at Nantworks at a speech at Stanford last night.” NantWorks brings together public and private businesses across healthcare, energy and communications. Soon-Shiong highlighted an antibody search engine he likened to Google, part of an effort to find and treat tumors more precisely. He said that the search engine will use camelid antibodies to make tumors visible on PET scans, then targeting them with radioactive isotopes. The goal is to connect cancer detection with treatment directed at the tumor. He also outlined a system that gives doctors real-time patient data to help them make timely treatment decisions. Soon-Shiong said the tech already had FDA approval, but did not name the product. Meanwhile, Soon-Shiong outlined tech to move data faster as AI systems grow. These include high-speed WiGig wireless tech and optical chips that transmit data using light. He also highlighted U.S. factories to make optical chips and chipsets that connect AI data centers. NantOptiFab is already working in this area, making chips in California that use light to carry information for AI networks, space systems and quantum technology. An SEC filing in August named Soon-Shiong as a director and showed that the company raised $20 million by selling shares to one unnamed investor. His space ambitions include chips for use in space, satellite terminals that communicate using light, and new ways to build and launch satellites. The projects also extend to energy, materials and food safety. Soon-Shiong listed batteries that work in Arctic conditions, non-toxic methods of making graphene, biodegradable alternatives to plastic made from ocean-derived materials, and machine vision to detect harmful substances in food and baby food at the point of purchase. Soon-Shiong also spotlighted a blockchain-based exchange for tokenized securities, or digital versions of stocks and other investments. He pitched it as a way to give companies and investors more control. In January, Nant Global Finance announced plans to bring stock trading, shareholder records and blockchain settlement onto one platform. Its acquisitions included Horizon Globex, which provides technology for the Upstream exchange, and BlockAgent and Equity Stock Transfer, which maintain shareholder records. The company also planned to rename Arkonis Capital, a brokerage and trading platform, NantX. At the time, completing its brokerage acquisitions still required approval from the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). Soon-Shiong also circled back to ImmunityBio’s work on IL-15, a protein that helps activate the body’s immune defenses. Its drug Anktiva stimulates natural killer cells and T cells, which fight cancer and infections. The company is testing whether it can help patients whose immune-cell counts are too low, a condition called lymphopenia. This also includes a sepsis trial that Soon-Shiong said had been authorized. “Trials will be starting soon in USA and Europe,” he said on Wednesday. The Phase 2 study will test Anktiva in about 50 critically ill adults with sepsis and low immune-cell counts. Researchers will compare the drug plus standard care with standard care alone to see whether it reduces deaths within 28 days. “Longevity at work. Book of our patients’ stories soon,” Soon-Shiong said. The drug is already approved in the U.S. with BCG for certain bladder cancers. ImmunityBio’s approval last month expanded its use to another group of patients whose cancer had not responded to BCG. The update comes shortly after ImmunityBio’s third-quarter results, which showed that net product revenue rose 53% from a year earlier to $48.7 million. For the first nine months, it grew 92% to $143.6 million. The company also said its Quilt-2.005 trial met its main goal in a group of bladder cancer patients who had not previously received BCG. The company is on track to seek expanded FDA approval for these patients in the fourth quarter. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) surged 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday after the company said that its key leukemia trial results are expected this month, with its CEO pointing to the treatment’s potential to become a “transformative” immunotherapy if successful. SLS stock fell nearly 5% on Thursday to $8.03, with shares on track to post their third straight weekly decline. The update is related to the Phase 3 Regal trial of Galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The November timeline narrows Sellas’ earlier guidance for results in the fourth quarter. “In our ongoing Phase 3 REGAL trial of GPS, we are focused on completing the final analysis following the announcement of 80th event, and we expect to announce topline primary endpoint results this month,” CEO Angelos Stergiou said. “If successful, we believe GPS could be a transformative new immunotherapy for AML patients in second complete remission.” Regal is testing GPS as a maintenance treatment for AML patients who have returned to remission after treatment for a relapse. The study’s main goal is to determine whether GPS helps these patients live longer. GPS is licensed from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and targets WT1, a protein found in a range of cancers. Sellas disclosed late last month that the trial had reached its prespecified 80th death, the milestone required to begin its final analysis. This process involves finalizing and reviewing the trial database, revealing treatment assignments and analyzing the results. Beyond GPS, Sellas is advancing its second leukemia drug, Tambiciclib, or SLS009, with investors looking ahead to fresh trial results and a major medical conference presentation. The company has enrolled 40 patients in its planned 80-patient Phase 2 study in newly diagnosed AML, up from 28 disclosed in August. The study includes patients whose disease stops responding early to Azacitidine and Venetoclax, an existing drug combination. Enrollment and treatment are currently continuing, with preliminary results expected in the fourth quarter. The development comes after a completed Phase 2 study in patients whose leukemia returned or failed to respond after prior Venetoclax-based treatment. Sellas will present the findings on Dec.14 at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. The study enrolled 62 patients and combined SLS009 with azacitidine and venetoclax. Across all doses, 34% of the 59 patients evaluated responded to treatment. At the dose of 30 milligrams twice weekly, 54% of patients with monocytic AML, a leukemia subtype, responded, with median survival of 5.8 months. Among patients with a TP53 mutation, 57% responded, with median survival of 8.8 months. Sellas ended September with $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $138.3 million in June. “With $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, we are well positioned to further advance these programs,” Stergiou said. Third-quarter (Q3) net loss widened to $10.1 million from $6.8 million a year earlier, while loss per share narrowed to $0.05 from $0.06. Meanwhile, research and development spending rose to $7 million from $4.2 million as Sellas prepared for a potential GPS approval application after Regal’s final analysis. Additionally, Sellas is preparing to study SLS009 in pancreatic cancer patients after laboratory findings presented in September. Working with the University of Wisconsin-Madison, researchers tested SLS009 in cancer models grown from patient tissue, including one resistant to Daraxonrasib. They also tested it alongside the experimental drug ZEN3694. Sellas said that the findings support further research into overcoming treatment resistance. However, patient trials are yet to begin. title: Chevron Q3 Earnings Surge on Strong Refining: Is the Stock a Buy Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: Chevron CorporationCVX posted a sharp increase in third-quarter 2026 earnings, as stronger refining margins and record U.S. refinery throughput helped lift profitability. The energy giant earned $9.9 billion, or $5.06 per diluted share, compared with $3.54 billion, or $1.82, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings reached $10.4 billion, or $5.28 per share. The strong results were accompanied by healthy cash generation, rising earnings estimates and continued shareholder returns. Chevron has also delivered better year-to-date share-price performance than integrated energy peers ExxonMobil Holdings CorporationXOM and Shell plc SHEL. Let's examine the factors supporting its investment case. Chevron's downstream business played a major role in its third-quarter earnings growth. The segment generated $4.93 billion in earnings, up from $1.14 billion a year earlier, benefiting from stronger refining margins and reliable operations. This improvement was particularly noticeable in the United States, where downstream earnings jumped to $3.59 billion from $638 million in the year-ago quarter. U.S. refinery crude throughput reached a record 1.09 million barrels per day, with capacity utilization approaching 98%. Chevron is also making better use of its existing refining infrastructure. At the Pasadena refinery, the company increased processing capacity by approximately 15% through debottlenecking improvements, adding throughput capacity at relatively little cost. These initiatives highlight Chevron's focus on getting more value from its assets. Much like ExxonMobil and Shell, Chevron's integrated operations allow it to participate across the energy value chain, with refining serving as an important contributor to overall earnings. Analysts have become more optimistic about Chevron's earnings outlook, as reflected in upward revisions of the consensus estimates. Over the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate trend for Chevron's 2026 earnings has risen 12.90%, while the same for 2027 has increased 22.85%. ExxonMobil's earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 have increased 12.60% and 15.45%, respectively. Shell has recorded corresponding increases of 13.69% and 10.64%. While all three companies have seen upward revisions, Chevron stands out for 2027, with its estimate increasing more sharply than those of both peers. The stronger revisions suggest growing confidence in Chevron's ability to sustain earnings performance. Its refining operations, disciplined spending and expanding production opportunities provide several potential drivers of future profitability. Chevron's valuation also merits attention. The stock trades at 11.76 times forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E), slightly below ExxonMobil's multiple of 12.13 times. Shell, meanwhile, trades at 8.91 times. Although Chevron commands a premium over Shell, the modest discount to ExxonMobil offers an interesting comparison, particularly given its recent earnings performance and improving analyst expectations. Chevron's combination of reliable operations, substantial cash generation and shareholder distributions provides support for its valuation. For investors looking to gain exposure to a diversified energy producer, CVX offers an appealing mix of earnings potential and financial stability. Chevron has also performed well in the stock market. Shares of CVX have gained approximately 39.8% year to date, ahead of ExxonMobil's 38.4% increase and Shell's 33.2% rise. That gives Chevron a lead of 1.4 percentage points over ExxonMobil and 6.6 percentage points over Shell. The share-price gains have come alongside strong refining profitability, solid cash generation and improving earnings expectations. These developments have helped strengthen Chevron's standing among major integrated energy companies. With analysts continuing to raise their earnings estimates, Chevron has additional fundamental support for its investment outlook. Chevron's cash-generating ability remains a key attraction. The company generated $16 billion in operating cash flow during the third quarter, while adjusted free cash flow reached $14.2 billion. The company returned $6 billion to its shareholders, comprising $3.5 billion in dividends and $2.5 billion in share repurchases. Chevron also reduced total debt by approximately $3.5 billion during the quarter, further strengthening its balance sheet. Its production operations continue to deliver encouraging results. U.S. output exceeded 2 million barrels of oil equivalent per day for the fifth consecutive quarter. Production in the Permian Basin remained around 1 million barrels of oil equivalent per day for the sixth straight quarter. Chevron is also positioning itself for future expansion. Its Venezuelan joint ventures are targeting approximately 600,000 barrels per day of gross production by 2031, creating another potential avenue for growth. Together, steady production, capital discipline and strategic investments provide a strong foundation for Chevron's longer-term prospects. Chevron's third-quarter results offer several reasons for optimism. Strong refining profitability, record U.S. crude throughput and substantial cash generation demonstrate the company's ability to make the most of its integrated operations. Rising earnings estimates, a competitive valuation relative to ExxonMobil and better year-to-date share-price performance than both XOM and SHEL further strengthen the investment case. Chevron's commitment to shareholder returns and its plans to expand production add to the positives. title: Exxon, Chevron, and Shell Just Reported. Here's What Each One Said About Where Oil Goes Next. - The Motley Fool
content: Uncertainty is the main issue in the oil market, but that doesn't mean that these integrated energy giants aren't making plans. ExxonMobil (XOM +0.48%), Shell (SHEL +1.33%), and Chevron (CVX +1.64%) have their fingers on the pulse of the global energy market. However, energy is a commodity, so the best these integrated energy giants can do is react to what is taking place around them. Right now, with energy prices high, that's leading to strong financial results. However, the key issue is the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East. This highly uncertain event has upended global energy markets, leaving energy companies and entire countries in flux. Here's what Exxon, Shell, and Chevron were thinking about when they discussed earnings. The big picture: Be prepared for continued uncertainty. Exxon reported strong third-quarter 2026 earnings, with GAAP earnings of $3.72 per share, up from $1.76 a year earlier. Adjusted earnings rose from $3.52 in the second quarter of 2026 to $4.23 in the third, a jump of 20% in a single quarter.  That highlights just how volatile the energy sector is today. And the company is very clear about where that volatility is coming from, noting that "The pace of recovery in the Middle East and the broader market environment remain critical uncertainties." Essentially, that hints that the company's outlook is for elevated energy prices if the conflict continues and lower prices if the conflict draws to an end. That's not a unique perspective; Shell and Chevron pretty clearly believe the same thing. Notably, Chevron, another of the world's largest energy companies, is making a specific change to address the issue by reducing leverage. After an analyst on the company's earnings call highlighted the strength of Chevron's balance sheet, the company made a point of saying it wasn't looking to change its capital priorities. Chevron's debt-to-equity ratio is 0.17x, second only to Exxon's 0.13x. That said, Chevron, Shell, and Exxon have all been reducing leverage. A key reason for Chevron's financial prudence is its inability to predict oil price movements. Management noted that oil prices ranged from $68 to $132, a huge $64-per-barrel spread in just the third quarter. Given that backdrop, it makes complete sense that balance sheet strength remains important. And since geopolitical conflict and investor sentiment around it are key drivers of oil prices today, being prepared for volatility is really the best thing any company can do. Somebody is going to make a fortune on Anthropic’s IPO. It probably won’t be regular investors waiting for the day it goes public. Unless investors know where to look. Because two companies anyone can buy today already own pieces of Anthropic. And one of them owns a piece of OpenAI, too. That said, there's a changing dynamic in the global energy market that will likely linger long after the Middle East conflict ends. Shell, for example, has been in discussions with customers that range from companies to entire countries. And an increasingly important issue is energy security. Essentially, the conflict in the Middle East has increased the importance of having access to oil and natural gas that come from economically and politically stable regions. To that end, Shell highlighted that it recently gave the green light to a large expansion of a liquefied natural gas export facility in Canada. That investment, made along with project partners, will double the size of the export facility. While the project won't be complete until the early 2030s, that actually speaks to the long-term change Shell expects in the market. And management clearly highlighted on its conference call that energy security issues may lead customers to be less price-conscious. Unfortunately, there's really no clear way to know what happens next with oil prices. That's very clear when you examine what Exxon, Chevron, and Shell are saying. However, for investors, the bigger takeaway is that these global energy giants are preparing for continued uncertainty. Being in a state of flux isn't easy, but Exxon, Chevron, and Shell are all preparing for the immediate impact of that uncertainty and the long-term changes it may bring to the global energy market.
